note: Prices and capabilities are checked against each vendor's own site. They go stale, and these go public — re-verify before any release. docs/COMPARISON.md is the long-form source.

apps.name: Boring Notch
apps.credit: Free, open source, and made by people doing the same thing for the same reason. If you only want music in the notch, it is a good answer and you should use it.
apps.difference: It stops at media. There is no clipboard history, no timer, no meeting controls and no system monitor — and those are most of what Perch is for.

apps.name: Seam
apps.credit: On-device voice-to-text, which Perch does not have at 1.0 and which is the hardest thing on our roadmap. If dictation is why you are here, Seam has it and we do not.
apps.difference: No clipboard history, and macOS 14 minimum. Perch runs on Ventura and is free.

apps.name: Alcove
apps.credit: The best motion in the category. Its HUD replacements are the reference implementation and its animation is better than ours at launch — that is a matter of iteration, and we are iterating.
apps.difference: No shelf, no clipboard, no meeting controls, and nothing on a Mac without a notch. Perch does the HUDs too, and gives you the other fifteen modules.

apps.name: NotchNook
apps.credit: The most polished of the paid apps, and the widest feature set — shelf, lyrics, shortcuts, appearance controls. It earns its place.
apps.difference: $25, or $3 a month, and no clipboard history at that price. Perch has clipboard history, a system monitor and a real camera module, for nothing.

apps.name: DynamicLake Pro
apps.credit: Window snapping from the notch is genuinely good, and its file shelf with AirDrop and format conversion is the one Perch's is measured against.
apps.difference: Its "clipboard" is file clips, not text history. Perch has both, plus the system monitor nobody in this list has.

apps.name: NotchBay
apps.credit: The cheapest paid option, and its in-call mute, camera and leave controls are the stickiest feature in the category. Its tray reads text out of copied screenshots, which is where Perch's OCR idea came from.
apps.difference: Its tray caps at 60 clips and you cannot change it; Perch defaults to 200 and you can. macOS 14 minimum against our 13.

apps.name: TopNotch
apps.credit: Solves the opposite problem, free, and does it perfectly: it blacks out the menu bar so the notch disappears. If that is what you want, it is the right tool.
apps.difference: It is not a notch app, it is an anti-notch app. Perch ships the same blackout as one setting, so you do not have to choose.
